profile.name: Fang Zhang
profile.title: Research Assistant Professor
profile.department: Department of Food Science and Nutrition
profile.bio: Dr. Fang Zhang's research centers on nucleic acid-based analytical and diagnostic methods. Her group designs and engineers nucleic acids not only to detect DNA and RNA, but also leverages functional nucleic acids (aptamers, DNAzymes, G-quadruplexes) and nucleic acid-guided proteins (CRISPR/Cas, TtAgo, Tas) to sense a broad range of targets. Integrating AI/machine learning, nanomaterials, and emerging protein tools, the group develops faster, simpler, and more cost-effective solutions across the One Health continuum — from plants, animals, food, and the environment to medical diagnostics.

research.statement: We develop nucleic acid-based analytical and diagnostic methods spanning the One Health continuum. Our work centers on nucleic acid analysis and design: building DNA/RNA detection methods, exploiting functional nucleic acids to sense non-nucleic-acid targets, and engineering nucleic acid-guided proteins for diagnostics. By integrating AI/machine learning, nanomaterials, and novel protein tools, we aim for faster, simpler, and cheaper solutions from plants and animals, food, and the environment to medical diagnostics.

directions.name: Nucleic acid analysis & functional nucleic acid biosensing
directions.desc: DNA/RNA detection methods; functional nucleic acids (aptamers, DNAzymes, G-quadruplexes) engineered to sense non-nucleic-acid targets.

directions.name: CRISPR/Cas & nucleic acid-guided protein diagnostics
directions.desc: Programmable CRISPR/Cas12a/Cas14a, TtAgo and Tas systems for ultrasensitive, field-deployable diagnostics.

directions.name: Nanomaterials & AI-enabled biosensing platforms
directions.desc: Nanomaterials, machine learning, and emerging protein tools for faster, simpler, and cheaper detection solutions.

research.vision: Advancing rapid, accessible and affordable diagnostics across the One Health continuum.
research.mission: Our group engineers functional nucleic acids — aptamers, DNAzymes, G-quadruplexes — and nucleic acid-guided proteins (CRISPR/Cas, TtAgo, Tas) to build faster, simpler and cheaper biosensing platforms. We integrate AI/machine learning and nanomaterials to serve plant, animal, food, environmental and medical diagnostics.
